If so, the current hanja would be an etymologically erroneous spelling.

The modern Standard Seoul form may be a result of [[hypercorrection]] provoked by less prestigious southern dialects that began to shift {{IPAfont|/hj-/}} to {{IPAfont|/sj-/}} in the late sixteenth century: cf. anti-southern hypercorrection of {{IPAfont|/t͡ɕi/}} to {{IPAfont|/ki/}} in {{ko-l|김치}}, {{ko-l|기와}}.

They nonetheless use {{lang|ko|슈지}}, however, which implies that it was not considered an innovation by these speakers.

{{lang|ko|휴지}} is first attested in the {{lang|ko|捷解新語 / 첩해신어}} (''{{w|Ch'ŏphae Sinŏ|Cheopae sineo}}''), 1676, a text which uses both {{lang|ko|휴지}} and {{lang|ko|슈지}} apparently without any semantic distinction.
